title: A polynomial splitting field is finite and normal
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $E/K$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $p\in K[X]$ be a nonconstant polynomial [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Suppose $p$ is a product of linear factors in $E[X]$ and $E$ is the smallest subfield of itself containing $K$ and all the roots of $p$ in $E$. Then $E$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] and $E/K$ is normal: every irreducible polynomial over $K$ with a root in $E$ splits into linear factors in $E[X]$. Here a polynomial is irreducible if it is nonconstant and cannot be expressed as a product of two polynomials of positive degree.

source.place: Tag 09HU, lemma-splitting-field, normality of the field generated by all roots; finite generation by algebraic roots in its construction. Exact Mathlib clauses: IsSplittingField.lean:126-132 and Normal/Basic.lean:63-84.

The hypothesis stated using field generation is exactly Polynomial.isSplittingField_iff_intermediateField at IsSplittingField.lean:178-183: splitting plus IntermediateField.adjoin of the root set equal to top. Its equivalence is already a Mathlib theorem, not a new identification. Normal means algebraicity and splitting of all minimal polynomials, Normal/Defs.lean:34-38.
